description:
Creates an intermediate [Upload](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/uploads) object
that you can add [Parts](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/uploads/subresources/parts) to.
Currently, an Upload can accept at most 8 GB in total and expires after an
hour after you create it.

Once you complete the Upload, we will create a
[File](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files) object that contains all the parts
you uploaded. This File is usable in the rest of our platform as a regular
File object.

For certain `purpose` values, the correct `mime_type` must be specified.
Please refer to documentation for the
[supported MIME types for your use case](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search#supported-files).

For guidance on the proper filename extensions for each purpose, please
follow the documentation on [creating a
File](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files/methods/create).

Returns the Upload object with status `pending`.

400.description: The upload request is invalid or exceeds a file size or storage quota limit.

429.description: Too many upload requests. Reduce the request rate and try again later.

bytes.description: The number of bytes in the file you are uploading.

filename.description: The name of the file to upload.

mime_type.description:
The MIME type of the file.


This must fall within the supported MIME types for your file purpose. See
the supported MIME types for assistants and vision.

purpose.description:
The intended purpose of the uploaded file.

See the [documentation on File
purposes](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files/methods/create#%28resource%29%20files%20%3E%20%28method%29%20create%20%3E%20%28params%29%200%20%3E%20%28param%29%20purpose%20%3E%20%28schema%29).

Upload.description: The Upload object can accept byte chunks in the form of Parts.

bytes.description: The intended number of bytes to be uploaded.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the Upload was created.

expires_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the Upload will expire.

file.description: The ready File object after the Upload is completed.

filename.description: The name of the file to be uploaded.

id.description: The Upload unique identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

object.description: The object type, which is always "upload".

purpose.description: The intended purpose of the file. [Please refer here](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files#%28resource%29%20files%20%3E%20%28model%29%20file_object%20%3E%20%28schema%29%20%3E%20%28property%29%20purpose) for acceptable values.

Upload.title: Upload

FileExpirationAfter.description: The expiration policy for a file. By default, files with `purpose=batch` expire after 30 days and all other files are persisted until they are manually deleted.

anchor.description: Anchor timestamp after which the expiration policy applies. Supported anchors: `created_at`.

seconds.description: The number of seconds after the anchor time that the file will expire. Must be between 3600 (1 hour) and 2592000 (30 days).

FileExpirationAfter.title: File expiration policy

OpenAIFile.description: The `File` object represents a document that has been uploaded to OpenAI.

bytes.description:
The size of the file, in bytes. In a completed file upload response, this can
be null when the file size is not yet available.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the file was created.

expires_at.description:
The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the file will expire. In a
completed file upload response, this can be null when no expiry is set.

id.description: The file identifier, which can be referenced in the API endpoints.

object.description: The object type, which is always `file`.

purpose.description: The intended purpose of the file. Supported values are `assistants`, `assistants_output`, `batch`, `batch_output`, `fine-tune`, `fine-tune-results`, `vision`, and `user_data`.

status.description: Deprecated. The current status of the file, which can be either `uploaded`, `processed`, or `error`.

status_details.description: Deprecated. For details on why a fine-tuning training file failed validation, see the `error` field on `fine_tuning.job`. Completed file upload responses can return null when these details are unset.

OpenAIFile.title: OpenAIFile

detailed_explanation.description: The public explanation for this block.

error_type.description: An optional classification; clients must accept additional values.

anyOf.description: An opaque target for explicitly continuing this review, or null when unavailable.
